doc.title: Albert Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: Basie's philosophy: play like you play
summary: Rowe reads a Basie quote from the book; Murray says Basie played within his range and outlasted bop.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Don’t think so. Well we have a couple of minutes before I know you have to move on. And I wanted to read one thing in your book from Basie, and just have you comment on it. This is something he said: “it’s the way you play it that makes it. What I say for Christ’s sakes, you don’t have to kill yourself to swing. Play like you play, play like you think, and then you got it, if you’re going to get it, and whatever you get, that’s you so that’s your story.” That was pretty much his philosophy on playing? That you don’t have to work that hard at it? Although he made it seem easy I guess.

Yeah. In other words he’s saying what is in your range, and you can extend yourself to see what your range is you see, then you don’t worry about what’s beyond that. Do the best you can within that. If you can do that then you’ve got it if you’re going to get it. If you’re not, you’re not. You see? So that he wasn’t likened to everything that came along at all. And sure enough, his stuff is, like I said right along, his is the durable stuff. And it turns out what he would use, let’s say there was bop. Basie was there before bop started. Basie was there when bop went out. Because how long did bop last? You know what I mean?
